clue.text: Lunatic presided over trial, having rejected coroner's conclusion

indicators.note: what is rejected is thrown out

parts.note: a judge who presided over a trial heard the case
the last letter of coroneR, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A deranged judge sits on a case after overruling the coroner's verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presided over trial' is the courtroom phrase HEARD CASE; take out its R and the judge becomes the madman.
explanation.definitionFit: A headcase is British slang for a crazy or unstable person.

clue.text: Rushes around married women's lodgings in Brunei

explanation.surface: Someone hurries round the accommodation of wives in a Sultan's state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rushes' looks like the reeds; it is the verb, to hare.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the women's quarters of a Muslim household, of the kind a Sultan of Brunei might keep.

clue.text: Gunners indisposed to block supply route

indicators.note: something blocking a route sits inside it

parts.note: an artery is a main road or supply route

explanation.surface: Sick soldiers are posted to cut off the enemy's supply line.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a military manoeuvre, which keeps 'supply route' looking literal rather than as a word for a main road.
explanation.definitionFit: The artillery is the arm of an army made up of gunners, as the Royal Artillery's men are called.

clue.text: Deciphering incomplete code could unlock a utopian realm

indicators.note: an incomplete word has lost its last letter
deciphering rearranges a coded text into a new order

explanation.surface: Cracking a partial code might open the way to a paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could unlock a' reads as the sentence's verb phrase, but every letter of it is fodder alongside COD.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloud-cuckoo-land, from Aristophanes' Birds, is an imaginary ideal realm of fanciful dreamers.

clue.text: Clergymen discovered hiding in ship's quarters

indicators.note: dis-covered means with the cover off, so the outer letters go
what is hiding in something sits inside it

parts.note: RECTORS with the cover (first and last letters) taken off

explanation.surface: Stowaway priests are found lurking in the crew's cabins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' reads as found out; split it as dis-covered, uncovered. 'Quarters' is not cabins but divisions.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a city's districts are its quarters, and the same parts of an area can be called its sectors.

clue.text: Dormant snake seen outside shelter

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side

explanation.surface: A hibernating snake is spotted lying outside its den.
explanation.walkthrough: The lee is the side sheltered from the wind, a sailing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant and asleep both mean inactive, at rest.

clue.text: Arbitrarily develop this fake reaction to someone's appearance

indicators.note: arranged arbitrarily means in no set order

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put on a false response when a person shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appearance' sounds like looks, but it means arriving: the phrase is what you say when the person you were discussing walks in.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Speak of the devil' is the remark made when someone just mentioned turns up.

clue.text: Run from sex trafficker

indicators.note: the answer is taken from inside the letters that follow

parts.note: the letters run from the second of 'sex' to the second of 'trafficker'

explanation.surface: An order to escape a sex trafficker.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an extra is a run not scored off the bat, such as a bye or wide.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a run credited to the batting side without the batter hitting it.

clue.text: Forecasts result in flipping bad mood

parts.note: a strop is a sulk, British slang
an end is a result, an outcome

explanation.surface: Predictions end up putting someone in a foul temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British swear word qualifying 'bad mood'; it is the reversal. A strop is a fit of sulky temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to signal in advance what is coming, though portends usually carries a sense of omen.

clue.text: Large hole right below chest

indicators.note: in a down entry, below means coming after

explanation.surface: A wound sits just beneath someone's ribcage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chest' invites anatomy; it is a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight description: the pit a bomb or meteor blasts into the ground.

clue.text: Relative value of empty apartment in city

indicators.note: emptied, the word keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: A and T, the outside of ApartmenT

explanation.surface: An estate agent weighs up what an unoccupied flat in town is worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relative value' sounds like property prices; it is the mathematical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A mathematical sense: one quantity measured against another, as three to one.

clue.text: Workman caught a tenant embracing Penny

explanation.surface: A builder is caught in a clinch with a lodger called Penny.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on 'Penny' dresses the coin as a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a tradesman who works in wood is one kind of workman.

clue.text: Awkward line in drama about ordinary company department

parts.note: taken as written, with the L put in it
O = ordinary, as in O level
the IT department of a company

explanation.surface: An actor fluffs a clumsy line in a play set in an office.
explanation.walkthrough: O for ordinary comes from the old British O level exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from French mal adroit, badly skilful: clumsy.

clue.text: King starts to notice an extremely versatile villain

indicators.note: the starts of the next two words are their first letters

parts.note: the first letters of Notice An

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A monarch begins to see that a rogue can play any part.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface knowingly nods at playing cards, where the knave sits next to the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, old-fashioned: the word for a scoundrel before it became the jack in a pack of cards.

clue.text: French article about strange, retiring creatures

indicators.note: retiring means going back

explanation.surface: A piece in a French paper about odd, shy animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' is the grammar kind, not a piece of writing. Rum is British for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are primates of Madagascar, retiring nocturnal creatures.

clue.text: Agitated rugby fan initially ran away

indicators.note: the fan's initial is its first letter

explanation.surface: An upset rugby supporter took off.
explanation.walkthrough: RU for Rugby Union is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from feathers or water disturbed out of their smooth state into a flustered one.

clue.text: Proprietor of farm, say, left warden no alternative

indicators.note: an alternative version of the letters is a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A farm owner left the gamekeeper without any choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No alternative' reads as no choice; 'alternative' alone is the anagram signal, and 'no' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The owner of a farm is one example of a landowner, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Thoughtful type has drink in a theatre

parts.note: NT = the National Theatre in London

explanation.surface: A pensive person takes a drink at the theatre bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' only joins the pieces. The definition is a pun: ruminate means to ponder, and a ruminant, like a cow, chews the cud.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruminant chews the cud, and ruminating is thinking hard, so it is a 'thoughtful type' in jest.

clue.text: Liberated Union State with adequate education

explanation.surface: A newly freed state of the American Union has a decent school system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union State' reads as one American state; it splits into U and NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Unyoked means freed from a yoke, liberated.

clue.text: Ruins two upstanding teachers

parts.note: says how many teachers to find; it gives no letters

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: SIR, how pupils address a teacher, and BED, a Bachelor of Education

explanation.surface: A pair of honest teachers spoils something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstanding' reads as honourable; in a down clue it turns the letters upward. 'Ruins' is a noun, not the verb the surface wants.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is the scattered remains, the ruins, of something destroyed.

clue.text: His Excellency leaves infidels' capital

parts.note: HE = His Excellency, the letters removed

explanation.surface: An ambassador departs a city of unbelievers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' is the verb depart, not foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Greek seat of government is one capital city among many.

clue.text: Nasal sound is audible in question

indicators.note: what is audible is heard, so the sound, not the spelling, counts

parts.note: atishoo is the sound of a sneeze

explanation.surface: A snuffle can be heard during questioning.
explanation.walkthrough: Atishoo is the British spelling of a sneeze, the American achoo.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: both phrases describe the matter currently being disputed.

clue.text: Twisted attorney suppressing perverse lust for 18-year-olds?

indicators.note: in a down entry, pressing down on something means sitting above it
perverse means turned awry, so the letters are turned too

explanation.surface: A corrupt lawyer covers up his own twisted desires for teenagers.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: at 18 you are legally an adult.
explanation.definitionFit: Eighteen-year-olds are adults in law, one example of the class.

clue.text: Illustration detailed embryo's last stage of development

indicators.note: de-tailed means with its tail cut off
the embryo's last is its final letter

explanation.surface: A textbook diagram shows an embryo at its final phase of growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like 'in detail'; read it as de-tailed.
explanation.definitionFit: The imago is the final, adult stage in an insect's development.

clue.text: Make reparations in agreement

definitions.meaning: a verb for making amends for a wrong

definitions.note: read as AT ONE, two words
definitions.meaning: a two-word idiom for agreeing, run together

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense needs the answer split in two: AT ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is a plain synonym for making amends; the second is the idiom for two parties who agree, read as two words.

clue.text: Dazzle female with vintage eyewear

explanation.surface: Someone wows a woman wearing retro glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eyewear' calls up spectacles; a blindfold is worn over the eyes too.
explanation.definitionFit: A blindfold is worn over the eyes, so it counts as eyewear, if a playful kind.

clue.text: Earl captivated by original Mona Lisa's enigmatic features

indicators.note: an original version is a newly made one, so the letters are made anew

explanation.surface: A nobleman is spellbound by the genuine Mona Lisa's mysterious face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Features' pulls toward the famous smile, and 'original' toward the real painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Anomalies are puzzling irregularities, features that cannot be explained.

clue.text: Records of victory in year fifty

explanation.surface: Accounts of a win in the year fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Records' reads as written accounts; it is the records you play.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinyl is a collective word for records, pressed from that plastic.

clue.text: Endeavour to squeeze butt in

parts.note: a butt is an end, as of a cigarette

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to push their backside through a narrow gap.
explanation.walkthrough: The last word, 'in', looks like the end of the instruction; it is the definition, meaning fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal sense: what is 'in' is currently in fashion.

clue.text: Condemns European resistance movement about obstructing detective

indicators.note: what obstructs something stands in the middle of it

explanation.surface: A wartime underground group in Europe denounces the police officer standing in its way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European resistance movement' reads as one wartime group; E is European, and the PLO is the resistance movement.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplore is to condemn strongly.
